Feck this is going to take a while and I will generalise with the main points you need to be aware of...

Bread recipes

One thing you will need is a decent bread tin.

They are not expensive and are worth the couple of $ "investment". Just go to a store that sells home equipment and ask. I say ask because you are at the beginning, the people in the store will be helpful.

Maybe a measuring jug and a decent size mixing bowl?

You will need yeast, flour and salt.

Salt

Salt any normal salt.

Yeast

Yeast, dry or live?

Go to the super market and ask for yeast, they will point you in the right direction. There are many arguments about dry or live yeast. I would say start with dry yeast and swap to live yeast later. Two or three packets, yeast is very cheap.

Start with either. You put yeast in warm water for a few minutes to let it activate. Warm. Not hot water. Hot water will kill the yeast.

Flour

Start with a simple white flour. Starting with a whole grain from day one will lead to frustration.
Go to the supermarket and maybe ask, it depends on what the stores are like where you are. You want a plain flour. Get two bags.

So now you have a bread tin, warm yeast, salt and flour.

Mix the ingredients together in the proportions of the recipes.

Leave to rise under a towel. This depends on how warm it is. Bread will rise differently in winter than in summer. Basically leave the bread mix till it is at least twice the size.

Once the bread has risen, take it out of the bowl cover the mix in flour and put in the bread tin. Let it rise some and then put in the oven as per the recipe.

I use what is called a wet mix. And it depends if I want a bread in the evening or morning.

As I say, I use a wet mix. I do not kneed the mix. I just stir it all together and leave it. I use cling film (or whatever you call it) to cover the bowl for rising. Then use a bread tin and cover that with a towel for the second rise

If I want a bread mix for the evening, I make a mix before work and leave it for the day and cook it off in the evening

If I want a bread mix for the day, I mix it the night before and let the bread rise overnight.

Once you have a good white bread mix that you like, the same mix can be used for pizza base, bread, rolls, pitta bread and brown bread.

Brown whole wheat is not difficult. You make a white mix and add the flour your want (wholegrain or whatever).
